about: I am a marine biologist and ocean researcher specializing in deep-sea biodiversity and Arctic ecosystem dynamics. With over a decade of fieldwork across the North Atlantic, I combine rigorous scientific methodology with a deep respect for the natural world. My research focuses on how warming ocean temperatures are reshaping the vertical migration patterns of deep-sea organisms — work that has direct implications for global carbon cycling and fisheries policy. I collaborate with international research institutions, publish in peer-reviewed journals, and am passionate about translating complex science into actionable conservation strategies.

experience.company: Marine and Freshwater Research Institute (MFRI), Reykjavík
experience.description: Lead investigator on the Arctic Deep-Sea Biodiversity Project, managing a team of 6 researchers and overseeing ROV-based sampling expeditions in waters up to 2,400m depth. Secured €1.2M in EU Horizon funding. Published 14 peer-reviewed papers in journals including Nature Oceans and Deep-Sea Research.

Conducted independent research on mesopelagic fish communities and diel vertical migration. Operated aboard R/V Atlantis for 3 research cruises. Co-developed a new acoustic tracking methodology now adopted by 12 international research stations.

experience.company: University of Iceland, Department of Life and Environmental Sciences
experience.description: Assisted with long-term monitoring of sub-Arctic benthic communities and contributed to environmental impact assessments for offshore energy projects. Mentored undergraduate field courses in marine ecology.

experience.company: Icelandic Institute of Natural History, Garðabær
experience.description: Supported coastal habitat surveys and marine mammal observation programs. Compiled species distribution data for the National Marine Biodiversity Database and contributed to public science communication campaigns.
